deepdive.sec: Integrated Steel & Precision Castings / Energy Transition

bull_bear.body: Priority on debt reduction (already substantially reduced), followed by organic capacity expansion (tubes, castings, mines). Merger of Oliver to consolidate earnings. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but cash generation exceeds investment needs.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) Commodity volatility (coal vs pig iron spread); 2) Execution risk on Solapur ramp-up ('ticklish' process stability); 3) Regulatory delays in renewable power slot utilization; 4) Global geopolitical disruptions affecting export logistics/pricing.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; focused on volume execution and cost control; transparent about operational hiccups (Hiriyur, Solapur complexity); confident in long-term structural shift to value-added products.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Solapur foundry underperformance is technical (core productivity/complexity of blocks/heads), not demand-driven; Oliver merger expected to close in 'couple of months' to capture FY26 benefits; Company targeting 90MW equivalent green power to market 'green steel' premium; Machining value-add to reach INR100cr within a year.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Gross Debt (Q1 FY27) of Rs 1,156 Cr on a standalone basis as on June 2026.
- Net Debt / EBITDA (Annualized) of 1.29x, with the deck defining "Net Debt = Gross Debt less cash and bank balances".
- Capex is directed at efficiency and green energy (Rs 131 Cr YTD FY27) plus capacity - the Solapur foundry line and machining capacity enhancement.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership position in the domestic casting business
- Shift toward high-complexity, high-precision castings (cylinder blocks/heads, critical engine parts) that few competing foundries can produce at the required quality/consistency, supporting resilient realisations
- Backward/forward integration across pig iron, steel, castings and tubes reducing exposure to any single commodity leg
- Captive renewable power (70 MW solar at Jalna running at full capacity plus 12 MW at Solapur) structurally lowering manufacturing cost independent of commodity price cycles
- Kirloskar Group parentage and brand
- Broad, growing OEM customer base in castings (29 customers, three added in FY26) with machining capability (80+ Machining Centres across three foundry locations)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sectoral risk — The Risk Management Committee's framework for identifying internal and external risks explicitly names 'sectoral' risk as a distinct category alongside financial, operational, sustainability/ESG, information and cyber security risks - reflecting KFIL's exposure to ferrous-industry cyclicality.
- Cybersecurity and information risk — On the Risk Management Committee's recommendation, the Risk Management Policy was formally amended during FY26 to explicitly add information and cyber-security risks (alongside ESG-related risks) to its scope, indicating management now treats these as material enough to warrant a policy update.
- Statutory / compliance risk — The Company's ERM framework formally classifies risks into five categories - strategic, operational, financial, statutory/compliance and reputational - with statutory/compliance risk (non-adherence to laws/regulations) treated as one of the standing top-level categories monitored by the Board and Risk Management Committee.
- Continuing financial support obligations to subsidiaries — During FY2025-26 the Company granted INR 33.15 Crores in loans to its subsidiaries for capital expenditure, refurbishment of plant and machinery, and working capital - an ongoing intra-group funding commitment (in addition to inter-company loans to erstwhile subsidiaries Oliver Engineering Private Limited and Adicca Energy Solutions Private Limited that were eliminated on their merger into KFIL).
- Legacy overseas holding-structure complexity — ISMT Enterprises SA (Luxembourg) was dissolved and deregistered effective 1 September 2025 as part of the Company's broader plan to wind up 'redundant overseas holding structures' inherited following its amalgamation of erstwhile domestic parent ISMT Limited, alongside the liquidation of ISMT Europe AB (Sweden) and Structo Hydraulics AB (Sweden, under liquidation) - indicating historical complexity in the international subsidiary structure that management is still unwinding.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Pig Iron: Sales 1.27L tons (Q4), realization down 6% YoY but pricing up INR4k/ton vs Dec; Castings: Sales 35k tons (Q4, +9%), realization flattish despite mix upgrade, FY27 target 1.85-1.9L tons; Tubes: Sales 51k tons (Q4), realization -10% YoY, capacity expansion to 4L tons planned; Steel: Sales 24.8k tons (Q4, +20%), moving towards alloy grade.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as "a leading integrated ferrous manufacturer and a key company within the diversified Kirloskar Group", operating "across the iron and steel value chain - from pig iron smelting to downstream castings, steel, and precision tubes - serving a broad base of industrial customers".
- Integration is the stated moat: "KFIL's integrated model provides a natural cost hedge: pig iron produced at blast furnaces feeds into casting operations, enabling margin stability across cycles."
- Constituent of the Kirloskar Group, "which has a legacy of over 136 years in Indian manufacturing" (Key Facts slide states the group as "Kirloskar Group (est. 1888)").
- Products listed as "Pig Iron | Castings | Steel | Tubes"; listed on NSE (KIRLFER) and BSE (500245).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] Oliver Engineering Private Limited and Adicca Energy Solutions Private Limited have been merged with the Company; prior-year presentation numbers are restated post-merger.
- [Deferred tax] A footnote on the 5-quarter trend slide refers to "Recognition of deferred Tax on unabsorbed depreciation and carry forward losses arising from Oliver and Adicca Merger."
- [Demand backdrop, sourced by the deck to external reports] The deck cites alloy steel consumption up "25.6% YoY to 3.0 million tonnes in Q1 FY27" and "26% YoY growth in passenger vehicles"; outlook stated as "Demand is expected to remain healthy, supported by infrastructure spending, rural recovery, and improving industrial activity."

business.body: KFIL is a diversified metals manufacturer with integrated operations spanning pig iron, grey iron castings, steel and seamless steel tubes. It supplies customised, high-precision castings (cylinder blocks/heads, critical engine components, complex earthmoving components) to automobile, tractor, construction-equipment and industrial-engine OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, multiple grades of pig iron to automobile, textile, pump, diesel-engine and pipe manufacturers, and steel/seamless tubes (including OCTG for oil & gas) to automobile, bearing, general-engineering and construction customers.

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~15% volume growth targeted for FY27; Margin: Trajectory improving from 12.5% towards 15% as price hikes pass through; Order Inflow: Strong in auto/TREM castings and oil-gas tubes; Capex: INR600-700cr/year planned (includes INR500cr for large tube mill, INR125-150cr for Hiriyur upgrade).

outlook.body: Castings: 3 new customers added (diesel engine, TREM, earthmoving); Tubes: Pending ONGC tenders expected, export demand robust due to global reconstruction; No specific tonnage guidance provided for pending orders.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: 1) Merger of Oliver Engineering (adds ~25k tons, INR250cr revenue run-rate by FY27); 2) Solapur foundry ramp-up to 5k tons/month (from 4.2k); 3) 6th & 7th foundry projects to hit 3L tons casting capacity; 4) Seamless tube expansion to 4L tons (+1.5L tons); 5) Hiriyur BF upgrade to 3L tons.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Three cost levers driving the business: green energy commissioning, blast furnace productivity improvement, and product-mix improvement
- In pig iron, reduce external sales of commodity pig iron over time, convert more hot metal internally into higher-value steel, and protect margins via value-added products
- Deliberately shift casting mix toward high-complexity, high-precision products (cylinder blocks/heads, complex earthmoving components, critical engine parts) that command better pricing and that fewer competing foundries can produce at the required quality/consistency
- Simplify corporate structure and unlock synergies via the NCLT-approved merger of Oliver Engineering Private Limited and Adicca Energy Solutions Private Limited into KFIL (effective 1 April 2025)
- Expand machined-castings capability (over 80 Machining Centres across Koppal, Solapur and Rajpura foundries) as a strategic priority
- Grow OCTG and premium tube products (currently ~10% of tube sales) to a much larger share of the mix as larger-diameter capacity is commissioned
- Maintain capex/project momentum through the commodity downturn rather than cutting investment - management view is that companies which cut capex in downturns miss the upturn
- Pursue backward integration into captive iron ore (Jambunatha mine bid) to secure foundry-grade ore supply
- Transform the Jejuri plant into a certified green-steel facility
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: KFIL states it kept every capex project running through the FY26 commodity downturn rather than cutting investment ("we did not stop a single project"), citing the Koppal steelmaking project, mines development, foundry expansions, and wind/solar additions as all remaining on track. In pig iron, the company plans to temporarily run at higher volumes (up to 7 lakh MT per annum) before external sales decline as the Koppal steelmaking project comes onstream and hot metal is redirected internally to the steel plant. In castings, a sixth foundry (a large casting facility) is being commissioned, and management says a seventh foundry will be needed in the next two to three years to meet order-book delivery obligations; casting volume is targeted to grow from ~1,53,000 MT to 1,75,000-1,80,000 MT in FY2027. In seamless tubes, the company is targeting expansion at Baramati to 4 lakh MT per annum (adding ~1,50,000 tonnes of new capacity to the existing 2,30,000 tonnes) over a two-to-three-year horizon, following debottlenecking/ramp-up of the Baramati and Ahilyanagar tube operations that reached an annualised run-rate of ~1.89 lakh MT of tube sales. In steel, the Koppal steelmaking project has all clearances and is underway, and the Jejuri rolling mill is being debottlenecked to reach 3 lakh MT of rolled output. Management states the aggregate capital programme for this multi-business expansion is approximately INR 2,000-2,500 Crores over the next three years, on top of INR 2,500 Crores already invested over the past five years. Separately, the Indian steel industry at large is described as continuing to invest in capacity expansion, value-added products and green steel, an area where KFIL cites its Product Carbon Footprint certification at the Jejuri plant.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian steel industry: crude steel production up over 10% YoY to ~168 million tonnes in FY26, installed capacity ~220 million tonnes on track for the 300-million-tonne 2030 national target; demand healthy across construction, railways, infrastructure and capital goods, with automotive and tractor manufacturing growth directly supporting demand for KFIL's pig iron and casting products
- Steel sector continues to face import-dependent coking coal costs, rupee depreciation and high iron ore prices as key input-cost variables for KFIL's pig iron and casting operations, alongside global trade uncertainty; long-term outlook remains positive on strong domestic demand and supportive policy
- Global seamless pipes and tubes market (~USD 133.12 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 215.46 billion by 2032 at a 7.12% CAGR) continues to see strong growth from infrastructure, industrial manufacturing, energy projects, automotive and oil & gas demand
- Indian automobile industry recorded its highest-ever annual sales in FY26 after seven years, with commercial vehicles up 12.6% to 10.80 lakh units; demand for high-quality engineering steel, seamless tubes and automotive-grade materials expected to remain strong
- Indian tractor industry crossed one million units in annual retail sales for the first time in FY26, growing ~18.55% YoY on favourable monsoons, improved farm income and rising mechanisation - the tractor sector accounts for KFIL's largest share of casting volumes and its demand remained strong through FY26
- Global Special Bar Quality (SBQ) steel market (~USD 13.03 billion in 2024, projected to reach ~USD 27.74 billion by 2034 at ~7.85% CAGR) driven by automotive, aerospace, industrial machinery, construction and energy demand
- India's iron ore production rose to ~289 million MT in FY24-25 from ~277 million MT the prior year, supported by rising demand from steel, infrastructure, construction, automotive and energy sectors
- Coking coal and metallurgical coke remain in high demand domestically, driven by the National Steel Policy's 300 MT capacity target, with domestic raw coking coal production targeting scale-up to 83 MT
- FY26 input-cost squeeze: iron ore costs remained stubbornly high despite weak pig iron prices; coal prices gave some relief but rupee devaluation partly neutralised the benefit; continued Chinese dumping of seamless tubes eroded pricing power in the line-pipe segment
- Pig iron, seamless tube and steel realisations all declined YoY in FY26 (pig iron ~-6%, seamless tubes ~-9%, steel ~-5%), a sustained multi-quarter commodity down-cycle management says required rethinking cost and volume management simultaneously
- Current order-book position for the next 3 years' delivery obligations in castings requires foundry capacity expansion (cited as the rationale for commissioning a sixth foundry and planning a seventh)
- Secured orders and started initial deliveries of OCTG/premium tube products (premium couplings and high-collapse casing pipes for the oil & gas sector)
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: KFIL is pivoting from commodity pig-iron exposure to high-margin complex castings and green seamless tubes, with FY27 volume growth guided at 15% driven by Oliver merger and Solapur ramp-up. Margin recovery is anticipated in Q1FY27 as commodity price hikes (pig iron +INR4k/ton) offset coal inflation, supported by INR90cr annualized power savings from new renewables.

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.

In seamless tubes, the company is targeting expansion at Baramati to 4 lakh MT per annum (adding ~1,50,000 tonnes of new capacity to the existing 2,30,000 tonnes) over a two-to-three-year horizon, following debottlenecking/ramp-up of the Baramati and Ahilyanagar tube operations that reached an annualised run-rate of ~1.89 lakh MT of tube sales. In steel, the Koppal steelmaking project has all clearances and is underway, and the Jejuri rolling mill is being debottlenecked to reach 3 lakh MT of rolled output. Management states the aggregate capital programme for this multi-business expansion is approximately INR 2,000-2,500 Crores over the next three years, on top of INR 2,500 Crores already invested over the past five years. risks.note: The Risk Management Committee's framework for identifying internal and external risks explicitly names 'sectoral' risk as a distinct category alongside financial, operational, sustainability/ESG, information and cyber security risks - reflecting KFIL's exposure to ferrous-industry cyclicality.

On the Risk Management Committee's recommendation, the Risk Management Policy was formally amended during FY26 to explicitly add information and cyber-security risks (alongside ESG-related risks) to its scope, indicating management now treats these as material enough to warrant a policy update.

The Company's ERM framework formally classifies risks into five categories - strategic, operational, financial, statutory/compliance and reputational - with statutory/compliance risk (non-adherence to laws/regulations) treated as one of the standing top-level categories monitored by the Board and Risk Management Committee.

risks.risk: Continuing financial support obligations to subsidiaries
risks.note: During FY2025-26 the Company granted INR 33.15 Crores in loans to its subsidiaries for capital expenditure, refurbishment of plant and machinery, and working capital - an ongoing intra-group funding commitment (in addition to inter-company loans to erstwhile subsidiaries Oliver Engineering Private Limited and Adicca Energy Solutions Private Limited that were eliminated on their merger into KFIL).

ISMT Enterprises SA (Luxembourg) was dissolved and deregistered effective 1 September 2025 as part of the Company's broader plan to wind up 'redundant overseas holding structures' inherited following its amalgamation of erstwhile domestic parent ISMT Limited, alongside the liquidation of ISMT Europe AB (Sweden) and Structo Hydraulics AB (Sweden, under liquidation) - indicating historical complexity in the international subsidiary structure that management is still unwinding.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Limited (KFIL), a Kirloskar Group company, is a vertically integrated ferrous manufacturer producing pig iron, grey iron castings, steel and seamless steel tubes for automotive, tractor, construction-equipment, industrial-engine and oil & gas customers across India and …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: KFIL is a diversified metals manufacturer with integrated operations spanning pig iron, grey iron castings, steel and seamless steel tubes. It supplies customised, high-precision castings (cylinder blocks/heads, critical engine components, complex earthmoving components) to automobile, tractor, construction-equipment and industrial-engine OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, multiple grades of pig iron to automobile, textile, pump, diesel-engine and pipe manufacturers, and steel/seamless tubes (including OCTG for oil & gas) to automobile, bearing, general-engineering and construction customers.

guidance.body: Revenue Growth: ~15% volume growth targeted for FY27; Margin: Trajectory improving from 12.5% towards 15% as price hikes pass through; Order Inflow: Strong in auto/TREM castings and oil-gas tubes; Capex: INR600-700cr/year planned (includes INR500cr for large tube mill, INR125-150cr for Hiriyur upgrade).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 1) Merger of Oliver Engineering (adds ~25k tons, INR250cr revenue run-rate by FY27); 2) Solapur foundry ramp-up to 5k tons/month (from 4.2k); 3) 6th & 7th foundry projects to hit 3L tons casting capacity; 4) Seamless tube expansion to 4L tons (+1.5L tons); 5) Hiriyur BF upgrade to 3L tons.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian steel industry: crude steel production up over 10% YoY to ~168 million tonnes in FY26, installed capacity ~220 million tonnes on track for the 300-million-tonne 2030 national target; demand healthy across construction, railways, infrastructure and capital goods, with automotive and tractor manufacturing growth directly supporting demand for KFIL's pig iron and casting products
- Steel sector continues to face import-dependent coking coal costs, rupee depreciation and high iron ore prices as key input-cost variables for KFIL's pig iron and casting operations, alongside global trade uncertainty; long-term outlook remains positive on strong domestic demand and supportive policy
- Global seamless pipes and tubes market (~USD 133.12 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 215.46 billion by 2032 at a 7.12% CAGR) continues to see strong growth from infrastructure, industrial manufacturing, energy projects, automotive and oil & gas demand
- Indian automobile industry recorded its highest-ever annual sales in FY26 after seven years, with commercial vehicles up 12.6% to 10.80 lakh units; demand for high-quality engineering steel, seamless tubes and automotive-grade materials expected to remain strong
- Indian tractor industry crossed one million units in annual retail sales for the first time in FY26, growing ~18.55% YoY on favourable monsoons, improved farm income and rising mechanisation - the tractor sector accounts for KFIL's largest share of casting volumes and its demand remained strong through FY26
- Global Special Bar Quality (SBQ) steel market (~USD 13.03 billion in 2024, projected to reach ~USD 27.74 billion by 2034 at ~7.85% CAGR) driven by automotive, aerospace, industrial machinery, construction and energy demand
- India's iron ore production rose to ~289 million MT in FY24-25 from ~277 million MT the prior year, supported by rising demand from steel, infrastructure, construction, automotive and energy sectors
- Coking coal and metallurgical coke remain in high demand domestically, driven by the National Steel Policy's 300 MT capacity target, with domestic raw coking coal production targeting scale-up to 83 MT
- FY26 input-cost squeeze: iron ore costs remained stubbornly high despite weak pig iron prices; coal prices gave some relief but rupee devaluation partly neutralised the benefit; continued Chinese dumping of seamless tubes eroded pricing power in the line-pipe segment
- Pig iron, seamless tube and steel realisations all declined YoY in FY26 (pig iron ~-6%, seamless tubes ~-9%, steel ~-5%), a sustained multi-quarter commodity down-cycle management says required rethinking cost and volume management simultaneously
- Current order-book position for the next 3 years' delivery obligations in castings requires foundry capacity expansion (cited as the rationale for commissioning a sixth foundry and planning a seventh)
- Secured orders and started initial deliveries of OCTG/premium tube products (premium couplings and high-collapse casing pipes for the oil & gas sector)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Pressure from coal (+$25/ton) and dollar (INR95) partially offset by pig iron price recovery (+INR4k/ton vs Dec). Power cost savings: INR70cr realized in FY26; additional INR45-90cr expected from new 60MW wind/solar capacity commissioning by Sep-26. Oxygen plant (150 TPD) and PCI increase to reduce coal consumption.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority on debt reduction (already substantially reduced), followed by organic capacity expansion (tubes, castings, mines). Merger of Oliver to consolidate earnings. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but cash generation exceeds investment needs.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: KFIL states it kept every capex project running through the FY26 commodity downturn rather than cutting investment ("we did not stop a single project"), citing the Koppal steelmaking project, mines development, foundry expansions, and wind/solar additions as all remaining on track. In pig iron, the company plans to temporarily run at higher volumes (up to 7 lakh MT per annum) before external sales decline as the Koppal steelmaking project comes onstream and hot metal is redirected internally to the steel plant. In castings, a sixth foundry (a large casting facility) is being commissioned, and management says a seventh foundry will be needed in the next two to three years to meet order-book delivery obligations; casting volume is targeted to grow from ~1,53,000 MT to 1,75,000-1,80,000 MT in FY2027. In seamless tubes, the company is targeting expansion at Baramati to 4 lakh MT per annum (adding ~1,50,000 tonnes of new capacity to the existing 2,30,000 tonnes) over a two-to-three-year horizon, following debottlenecking/ramp-up of the Baramati and Ahilyanagar tube operations that reached an annualised run-rate of ~1.89 lakh MT of tube sales. In steel, the Koppal steelmaking project has all clearances and is underway, and the Jejuri rolling mill is being debottlenecked to reach 3 lakh MT of rolled output. Management states the aggregate capital programme for this multi-business expansion is approximately INR 2,000-2,500 Crores over the next three years, on top of INR 2,500 Crores already invested over the past five years. Separately, the Indian steel industry at large is described as continuing to invest in capacity expansion, value-added products and green steel, an area where KFIL cites its Product Carbon Footprint certification at the Jejuri plant.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; focused on volume execution and cost control; transparent about operational hiccups (Hiriyur, Solapur complexity); confident in long-term structural shift to value-added products.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership position in the domestic casting business
- Shift toward high-complexity, high-precision castings (cylinder blocks/heads, critical engine parts) that few competing foundries can produce at the required quality/consistency, supporting resilient realisations
- Backward/forward integration across pig iron, steel, castings and tubes reducing exposure to any single commodity leg
- Captive renewable power (70 MW solar at Jalna running at full capacity plus 12 MW at Solapur) structurally lowering manufacturing cost independent of commodity price cycles
- Kirloskar Group parentage and brand
- Broad, growing OEM customer base in castings (29 customers, three added in FY26) with machining capability (80+ Machining Centres across three foundry locations)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: 1) Commodity volatility (coal vs pig iron spread); 2) Execution risk on Solapur ramp-up ('ticklish' process stability); 3) Regulatory delays in renewable power slot utilization; 4) Global geopolitical disruptions affecting export logistics/pricing.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Solapur foundry underperformance is technical (core productivity/complexity of blocks/heads), not demand-driven; Oliver merger expected to close in 'couple of months' to capture FY26 benefits; Company targeting 90MW equivalent green power to market 'green steel' premium; Machining value-add to reach INR100cr within a year.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Three cost levers driving the business: green energy commissioning, blast furnace productivity improvement, and product-mix improvement
- In pig iron, reduce external sales of commodity pig iron over time, convert more hot metal internally into higher-value steel, and protect margins via value-added products
- Deliberately shift casting mix toward high-complexity, high-precision products (cylinder blocks/heads, complex earthmoving components, critical engine parts) that command better pricing and that fewer competing foundries can produce at the required quality/consistency
- Simplify corporate …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:

- [Deferred tax] A footnote on the 5-quarter trend slide refers to "Recognition of deferred Tax on unabsorbed depreciation and carry forward losses arising from Oliver and Adicca Merger."

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
